reasons: The excerpt identifies a subscription price jumping at cart and says late disclosure of total cost can cause abandonment. It specifically recommends split testing and monitoring when pricing is not transparent up front.
The excerpt expressly says one-page versus multi-step checkout is something that needs to be split tested, while characterizing one-page conversion performance as based on the speaker's data.

The excerpt describes displaying a free-shipping-threshold callout to encourage an upsell and address concerns about extra costs. The candidate does not impose the example $12 or $75 threshold as a universal rule.
The good-checkout example includes Shop Pay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay, and the excerpt identifies a lack of accelerated checkout options as a checkout leak.
The excerpt says the good checkout defaults to guest checkout and contrasts this with forced account creation as a leak.
The excerpt recommends essentials-only address fields, calls unnecessary extra fields bloated, and qualifies reducing information by retaining what is needed to verify a genuine transaction.
The general advice to make returns prominent rather than hidden is supported.

The completion criterion improperly makes “30-day free returns” a required outcome. The excerpt presents that duration and free-return policy as an example “in this case,” not as a universal requirement.
The excerpt explicitly states that express checkout is at the top and says it should always be there.
The excerpt contrasts a checkout that sends email and SMS abandonment flows with one that does not.
The excerpt specifically warns that newly layered shipping, tax, and handling charges add costs at checkout and says this will tank conversion rates.
The excerpt says enough conversion and session volume is needed before trusting a claimed 10–20% lift and rejects a two-week result with about 100 conversions as a win.

The candidate preserves the malformed conversion-count transcription as an explicit unknown rather than certifying a specific number. The stated 40,000-session figure is expressly in the excerpt for the stated 2.5% conversion-rate example.

The excerpt says repeatedly checking tests and stopping when results appear significant inflates false positives, and says tests should run until they reach statistical relevance for the session volume.

The excerpt warns that Klaviyo campaign traffic can artificially spike conversion and revenue metrics and contaminate a landing-page test. It recommends custom landing pages driven only by cold Meta traffic in this testing context.

The excerpt says cold-Meta landing-page tests can remain flawed when time to purchase is extended because some customers convert after multiple clicks and potentially across channels. It does not supply a complete correction method, which the candidate accurately identifies as unknown.

The excerpt says scalable VSSL and long-form unaware targeting should be matched with a landing page rather than a product page, with the stated exception for a product page heavily manipulated to function almost as a landing page.

The excerpt gives the listed sequence—hook, problem, mechanism, objections, proof, risk reversal, and CTA—as the generic landing-page structure and says it is also how a VSSL script should be structured.

omissions.description: Avoid substituting unnecessary trust badges for actual checkout trust signals.
omissions.quote: We don't have all these unnecessary trust badges as well.

omissions.description: Where tax is already included in the original price, clarify that it is not an added charge; the excerpt also allows removing, minimizing, or relabeling the tax presentation to make this clear.
omissions.quote: The tax was inclusive within the original pricing. We're just breaking this out for them to clearly. So, we're just reinforcing that we're not actually charging them extra and that that's included. However, I also understand just removing that or minimizing it or changing the language to be able to make it clearer that we're not charging them extra.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins and ends mid-sentence, so adjacent context is unavailable.

The source is a spoken/transcribed passage with transcription defects, including “a,000 conversions,” “conversion left,” and “Clavio”; the intended exact conversion threshold cannot be established from this excerpt.
Several recommendations are explained through an unseen left-versus-right visual example, so the exact layouts and referenced labels cannot be independently inspected.
Performance claims are attributed to the speaker’s data or experience and are not accompanied here by study design, dates, definitions, or underlying measurements.
